html:
The Lingqu is a canal in Guangxi, southern China, built in 214 BCE under Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor. It is one of the oldest contour canals in the world.

It joins two river systems that flow in opposite directions: the Xiang River, which runs north to the Yangtze, and the Li River, which runs south toward the Pearl River and Guangzhou. The canal follows the hills for about 36 kilometres, and a stone divider at its head splits the water between the two branches.

Its first purpose was war. The Qin armies were invading the lands of the Baiyue peoples in the far south and needed supplies by boat. With the canal, ships could travel from the Yangtze to the south coast. The conquest gave China the far south for the first time, though after Qin fell it broke away as the kingdom of Nanyue until the Han conquest. Later dynasties added gates to manage the water. Like the Dujiangyan, it is still in use.
sum: The Lingqu is a canal in Guangxi, southern China, built in 214 BCE under Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor. It is one of the oldest contour canals in the world.
